metadata.title: Why Cold Energy Settles: A Tethered Medium Whose Displacement Is the Gravitational Polarization (Working Note)
metadata.description:
Working note, version 1.2 (2026-10-21; v1.1 and v1.0 2026-10-20; drafted 2026-10-14). AI-assisted research programme; not peer reviewed. kappa = 1/2 is fitted; the theory is not closed.

Correction (v1.1; wording fixed in v1.2): the exact static solution needs negative cold-energy density in a thin pancake through the saddle between two bodies (-89 times the mean cold density at R = 0.2 d for a Milky-Way-M31-like pair, -33 for a cluster pair, canonical footing). A medium of positive mass cannot supply this, so near field null points the cold energy must depart from the law. The total column through the saddle is still positive (negative part -0.206, net +0.016 in the solution's units), so neither picture predicts negative convergence there. Prediction: no saddle dip. Under the law the column through the saddle drops almost to zero in a narrow band; a positive medium cannot dig the part below zero density, a missing depth of 1.9 to 2.1 Msun/pc^2 (Milky-Way-M31-like pair) and 4.6 to 5.1 Msun/pc^2 (cluster pair). Published stacked lensing of luminous-red-galaxy pairs (arXiv:1702.08485) cannot test this yet (S/N below 1; about twelve times as many pairs needed). v1.1 called this "no negative lensing trough"; that wording was imprecise. The numbers are unchanged.

Galaxy rotation curves follow one relation between observed and baryonic acceleration, and in this framework its scale is set by dark energy, a0 = (1/2) c sqrt(G rho_DE). Clusters and the cosmic web also need a cold, collisionless mass component, 'cold energy', with Omega_c/Omega_b = 5.364 (measured). This short note explains why that component arranges itself, galaxy by galaxy, into exactly the profile the relation demands.

Cold energy is treated as a medium of real rest mass whose displacement P is the gravitational polarization. With K = 4 pi G and u = K|P|, the action is L = -|grad Phi - K P|^2/(2K) - rho_b Phi - W_rem(u) - (gamma/2)|grad P|^2, with K dW_rem/du = u^2/(a0 - u) and gamma = K L*^2/2. Varying Phi gives the baryons' Newtonian flux; varying P balances the baryons' inward pull g_N against the vacuum's push-back u^2/(a0 - u). The unique rest state is g_N = g^2/(g + a0), the simple interpolating function.

The stiffness length L* lies between 24 pc (set by Newtonian outer-halo globular clusters) and about 1 kpc. It screens the Solar System: Cassini's quadrupole is at most 5e-8 of the 2026 bound and the only residue is a uniform sunward pull of at most 2.4e-16 m/s^2. With catchment supply and condensed-only sourcing, the framework's own 1024^3 simulations are consistent with raw KiDS-1000 cosmic shear on both footings (Delta chi^2 -7.70 and -7.18 against a same-pipeline control) with inherited initial conditions; rerun with the framework's own initial conditions, the canonical footing still passes (Delta chi^2 -10.08), while the alternative-footing rerun is queued. An earlier own-supply rule is excluded by isolated-galaxy lensing, and an expelled-gas rule for hot-gas systems fails on the full 318 eRASS1 clusters.

Not derived: kappa = 1/2, Omega_c/Omega_b, L*, why only condensed baryons tether, and the relativistic completion. Sealed kill lines: a Cavendish test at four times the source acceleration (|dG/G| < 1e-6), a probe beyond 1000 AU (no non-thermal anomaly at or above 1e-13 m/s^2), and Gaia DR4 wide binaries (Newtonian). AI assistance: Anthropic's Claude, with review by parallel AI sessions.
